{{nihongo|'''Kuroshima Shrine'''|黒嶋神宮}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iyo Province]].

'''Kuroshima Jingū''' (くろしまじんぐう / くろしまじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Niihama|ar|نيهاما (إهيمه)|azb|نی‌ایهاما، اهیمه|be|Нііхама|ce|Ниихама|ceb|Niihama (lungsod)|cs|Niihama|de|Niihama|eo|Niihama|es|Niihama (Ehime)|fa|نی‌ایهاما، اهیمه|fi|Niihama (Ehime)|fr|Niihama (Ehime)|gl|Niihama|he|ניאיאמה|hu|Niihama|id|Niihama, Ehime|it|Niihama|ja|新居浜市|ko|니이하마시|lt|Nijihama|mg|Niihama|ms|Niihama, Ehime|mzn|نی‌ایهاما، اهیمه|nl|Niihama|no|Niihama|pl|Niihama|pt|Niihama|ro|Niihama|ru|Ниихама|sh|Niihama|simple|Niihama|sr|Нихама|sv|Niihama|tg|Нииҳама|tl|Niihama|tr|Niihama|tt|Ниихама|tum|Niihama|uk|Ніїхама|ur|نیہاما، اہیمے|uz|Niihama|vi|Niihama, Ehime|war|Niihama, Ehime|zh|新居濱市|zh_classical|新居濱市|zh_min_nan|Niihama-chhī|zh_yue|新居濱|qid=Q386628}}, {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|Q123376|qid=Q123376}}. It is identified with Kuroshima Shrine, a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}, and its former rank was prefectural shrine.

It enshrines {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Ōyamatsumi|Q386563|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamazumi-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|az|Konohanasakuya|ca|Konohana no Sakuya hime|de|Konohanasakuyahime|fa|کونوهاناساکویا-هیمه|fr|Konohana-no-Sakuya|it|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|コノハナノサクヤビメ|ko|고노하나노사쿠야비메|mni|ꯀꯣꯅꯣꯍꯅꯁꯀꯨꯌ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Konohanasakuya-hime|ru|Коноханасакуя-химэ|sv|Konohanasakuyahime|th|เซ็นเง็ง|vi|Konohana Sakuya Hime|zh|木花開耶姬|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohanasakuyahime}}, and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|es|Ame-no-minaka-nushi-no-kami|fa|آمه-نو-میناکانوشی|fr|Ame-no-Minakanushi|id|Ame-no-Minakanushi|it|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯅꯀꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Amenominakanushi|ru|Амэноминакануси|simple|Ame-no-Minakanushi|uz|Ame-no Minakanusi|zh|天之御中主神|qid=Q2842779}} as principal deities.

Kuroshima, where this shrine stands, is now connected to land, but was formerly an island. It is said to have been called Kuroshima because the island’s trees were densely dark.

=== Origin ===
[[File:Kursimazinɡu 0ɨ.jpg|thumb|Main sanctuary]]
It has long been revered for safe childbirth by the divine virtue of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Konohanasakuyahime}} and has been deeply worshipped from old times as a regional and safe-childbirth guardian deity. The exact founding is unknown, but because of traditions such as those about {{ill|Princess Ōku|de|Ōku no Himemiko|fa|شاهدخت اوکو|fr|Ōku|ja|大来皇女|sh|Princeza Ōku|zh|大來皇女|zh_classical|大來皇女|qid=Q985739}}, it is thought the initial enshrinement is old, around the Nara period. (When Prince Naka no Ōe, later {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ar|الإمبراطور تينجي|azb|تنجی (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Tenji|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر تێنجی|cs|Tendži|de|Tenji|es|Tenji Tennō|fa|امپراتور تنجی|fi|Tenji|fr|Tenji (empereur)|hak|Tenji Thiên-fòng|he|טנג'י|hu|Tendzsi japán császár|id|Kaisar Tenji|it|Tenji|ja|天智天皇|ka|ტენძი|ko|덴지 천황|nl|Tenji|pl|Tenji|pt|Tenji|ru|Император Тэндзи|sh|Car Tenji|simple|Emperor Tenji|sl|Cesar Tendži|sr|Car Tenji|sv|Tenji|th|จักรพรรดิเท็นจิ|tl|Emperador Tenji|tr|Tenji (imparator)|uk|Імператор Тендзі|uz|Imperator Tenji|vi|Thiên hoàng Tenji|wuu|天智天皇|yo|Emperor Tenji|zh|天智天皇|zh_min_nan|Tenzi Thian-hông|zh_yue|天智天皇|qid=Q314802}}, went to the {{ill|Battle of Baekgang|ca|Batalla de Baekgang|es|Batalla de Baekgang|eu|Baekgango gudua|fa|نبرد بکگانگ|fr|Bataille de Hakusukinoe|id|Pertempuran Baekgang|it|Battaglia di Baekgang|ja|白村江の戦い|ko|백강 전투|ms|Pertempuran Baekgang|no|Slaget ved Baekgang|pt|Batalha de Baekgang|ru|Битва на реке Пэккан|sh|Bitka kod Baekganga|tr|Baekgang Muharebesi|uk|Битва при річці Пек|vi|Trận Bạch Giang|zh|白江口之战|qid=Q608727}} in response to aid requests from Baekje remnants after {{ill|Paekche|ar|مملكة بايكتشي|ast|Baekje|az|Pekçe krallığı|azb|باکچه شاهلیغی|be|Пэкчэ|bg|Пекче|br|Baekje|ca|Paekche|cdo|Báik-cá̤|ckb|بایکجی|cs|Päkče|da|Baekje|de|Baekje|eo|Baekje|es|Baekje|eu|Baekje|fa|بکجه|fi|Baekje|fr|Baekje|gl|Baekje|hi|बेकजे|hr|Baekje|hu|Pekcse|id|Baekje|io|Baekje|it|Baekje|ja|百済|ka|პექჩე|km|បែកជេ|ko|백제|ku|Keyaniya Baekjeyê|lv|Pekče|mk|Пекче|mn|Пэгжэ|ms|Baekje|my|ဘက်ကျယ်|mzn|بیکچه|nl|Paekche|no|Baekje|pl|Baekje|pt|Baekje|ro|Baekje|ru|Пэкче|sh|Baekje|si|බෙක්ජේ|simple|Baekje|sr|Пекче|sv|Baekje|sw|Baekje|th|อาณาจักรแพ็กเจ|tl|Baekje|tr|Baekje|uk|Пекче|uz|Pekche|vi|Bách Tế|wuu|百济|zh|百济|zh_classical|百濟|zh_min_nan|Pek-chè|zh_yue|百濟|qid=Q28428}} fell to the allied forces of {{ill|Tang dynasty|Q9683|qid=Q9683}} and {{ill|Silla|Q28456|qid=Q28456}}, his pregnant consort Ochino-iratsume accompanied him. It has long been told in this area that when labor pains started in Ōku sea of the {{ill|Seto Inland Sea|Q231312|qid=Q231312}} (present {{ill|Hiuchi Sea|Q11569288|qid=Q11569288}}), they stopped at Kuroshima to pray for safe childbirth, and she safely gave birth to {{ill|Princess Ōta|Q603057|qid=Q603057}}.)
In the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012}}, it was treated as an imperial-prayer site of the {{ill|Southern Court|Q3001082|qid=Q3001082|lt=Southern Court}}. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, as one of six prayer shrines of the Saijō domain, it received a grant of 2 koku.

=== Subsidiary shrines ===
A belief says that when visiting for prayers, one takes home one safe-childbirth stone, and after a safe delivery returns two stones in thanks; then the child will grow healthy.

Kuroshima Jingū’s origin is ancient, and like Ōashi-chihime Shrine and Ta Shrine in the Kawahigashi area of Niihama, it is said to date to the Nara period.

As “Kuroshima Shrine camellia grove,” it was designated a Niihama City natural monument on December 5, Shōwa 60.

All three torii collapsed due to the Geiyo earthquake (March, Heisei 13). The following year (Heisei 13), one new steel torii was erected.

=== Subsidiary shrines ===
[[File:Kurosimazingu daimatuzinzya20220128.jpg|140px|thumb|Ōmatsu Shrine]]
* Tenjin Shrine: deity Sugawara no Michizane
* Inari Shrine: deity Inari-no-Kami
* Matsuo Shrine: deity Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami
* Iwanagahime Shrine: deity Iwanagahime-no-Kami
* Sarutahiko Shrine: Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto
* Wakamiya Shrine: various deities including Wakamiya, also called Okō-gami-san
* Ōmatsu Shrine: guardian deity of forests, in the mountain behind the main sanctuary
